skill.name: memory-init

content.value_statement: AI assistants often lose project context between sessions. This skill creates local memory files and clear routines for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Checks for existing CLAUDE.md, AGENT.md, MEMORY.md, and memory/ before initializing.
Collects project purpose, user role, assistant use, style preferences, and work habits.
Generates CLAUDE.md with project context, persona, conversation style, thinking priorities, and memory protocol.
Optionally creates AGENT.md with the same instructions for Codex.
Creates an initial MEMORY.md template for long-term facts and decisions.
Creates a memory/ directory and can add a first daily note with user approval.
limitations: Works only with files in the current project directory.
Does not synchronize memory across devices or repositories.
Generated memory files may contain sensitive details if users provide them.
Existing files require careful review before overwrite or reset.

use_cases.title: Start Project Memory
use_cases.description: Create local memory files before using Claude Code or Codex in a new repository.

use_cases.title: Standardize Context
use_cases.description: Give assistants a consistent project profile, user role, style preference, and memory workflow.

use_cases.title: Capture Daily Decisions
use_cases.description: Record useful decisions and context in daily memory notes during ongoing work.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Run /memory-init in this project. Ask me the setup questions and create the memory files after I answer.

prompt_templates.title: Add Codex Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up project memory and include AGENT.md for Codex if I confirm the generated CLAUDE.md content.

prompt_templates.title: Protect Existing Files
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this directory for existing memory files. Tell me what exists before adding missing files or overwriting anything.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Tailored Memory Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Initialize memory for this project. Infer the project summary from files, then tailor persona, style, priorities, and daily memory rules.

output_examples.input: Initialize memory for a new code project.
output_examples.output: The assistant asks for project purpose, role, usage, style, and habits, then creates local memory files after confirmation.

output_examples.input: Add memory support for Claude Code and Codex.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates Claude instructions, asks whether Codex is used, and adds matching Codex instructions only when approved.

output_examples.input: This project already has memory files.
output_examples.output: The assistant lists existing files, explains options, and asks whether to preserve, complete, overwrite, or reset them.

best_practices: Review generated CLAUDE.md and AGENT.md before relying on them.
Keep MEMORY.md focused on stable facts, decisions, and preferences.
Avoid storing secrets, credentials, or private customer data in memory files.
anti_patterns: Do not overwrite existing assistant instruction files without review.
Do not use daily memory notes as a full task tracker.
Do not store sensitive data that should stay outside repository files.

faq.question: What files does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates CLAUDE.md, MEMORY.md, memory/, and optionally AGENT.md for Codex.

faq.question: Does it use global Claude memory?
faq.answer: No. The skill directs assistants to use project-local files and avoid the global ~/.claude/ directory.

faq.question: Can it work in an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for existing memory files and asks before overwriting or resetting them.

faq.question: Is AGENT.md always created?
faq.answer: No. The skill asks whether Codex support is needed before creating AGENT.md.

faq.question: What should I put in MEMORY.md?
faq.answer: Use it for stable facts, preferences, project context, and important decisions.

faq.question: Can daily notes include sensitive information?
faq.answer: They can if you provide it. Avoid secrets, credentials, and private data in repository memory files.
